Hex-bin a rate (point count per areal-interpolated denominator)

Source: R/hex_bin_rate.R
mysterymaps_hex_bin_rate.Rd

Builds a hexagonal grid over boundary_sf, counts points_sf per cell (the numerator), area-weight interpolates denominator_sf[[denominator_col]] onto the same grid (the denominator – e.g. population), and returns both plus the resulting rate. This is the exact composition mysterymaps_hex_bin_counts() was deliberately left out of (a raw point count has no denominator to divide by): a rate needs a second, spatially-different data source, and getting that second source onto the same grid as the first is areal interpolation, not point-counting.

Usage

mysterymaps_hex_bin_rate(
  boundary_sf,
  points_sf,
  denominator_sf,
  denominator_col,
  per = 1,
  cellsize = 0.3,
  min_denominator = 0,
  value_col = "rate"
)

Arguments

boundary_sf

sf: polygon(s) defining the study area the grid is built over and clipped to.

points_sf

sf: point data to count per hex cell (the numerator).

denominator_sf

sf: polygon layer carrying the denominator (e.g. census tracts with a population column). Does not need to share boundary_sf's or points_sf's CRS; transformed automatically.

denominator_col

character(1): numeric column in denominator_sf to interpolate (e.g. "female_pop").

per

numeric(1): rate denominator scale, e.g. 100000 for "per 100,000". Default 1 (a plain proportion).

cellsize

numeric(1): hexagon size in the units of boundary_sf's CRS (degrees, if left in EPSG:4326). Default 0.3.

min_denominator

numeric(1): cells whose interpolated denominator falls below this are reported with rate = NA rather than a rate – a cell with a handful of interpolated residents produces a wild, near-meaningless rate (one point in a 40-person cell reads as 2,500-per-100k). Default 0 (no suppression; set this per study, the way mysterymaps_accessibility_map()'s caller would set a population floor).

value_col

character(1): name of the output rate column. Default "rate".

Value

An sf of every hex cell in the grid, carrying count (integer, numerator), denominator (numeric, interpolated), and value_col (numeric, NA where denominator < min_denominator).

Details

Unlike mysterymaps_hex_bin_counts(), which drops cells below min_count entirely, this function returns every cell in the grid, including zero-count and zero-denominator ones – a rate map needs the full grid to tell "no people live here" (denominator near zero, rate correctly NA) apart from "people live here and nothing was counted" (denominator present, count zero, rate correctly 0) apart from "people live here and some things were counted" (a positive rate). Collapsing any of those three into either of the others is the error mysterymaps_jenks_zero_scale() exists to prevent, and this function's output is built to feed that scale directly.

Denominator interpolation assumes the denominator is uniformly distributed within each denominator_sf polygon – the standard areal-interpolation assumption (sf::st_interpolate_aw(), extensive = TRUE, appropriate because a population count is additive: a hex covering half a tract is assumed to hold half that tract's people). It is weakest where the denominator is not actually uniform within a polygon, which it rarely is exactly – the same caveat as any choropleth built on areal units coarser than the thing being counted.

A point that lands exactly on a shared edge between two hex cells is counted in both – an inherent property of intersecting points against a sf::st_make_grid() lattice, shared with mysterymaps_hex_bin_counts() and mm_honeycomb_counts(). Negligible for real geocoded coordinates (probability zero in practice); a hazard only for hand-constructed or deliberately round test/example coordinates.

See also

mysterymaps_hex_bin_counts() for a plain count with no denominator; mysterymaps_jenks_zero_scale() to colour the result.

Other geospatial: mm_area_in(), mm_honeycomb_counts(), mysterymaps_hex_bin_counts(), validate_sf_inputs()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
boundary_sf <- sf::st_sf(geometry = sf::st_sfc(
  sf::st_polygon(list(cbind(c(-100, -97, -97, -100, -100), c(39, 39, 42, 42, 39)))),
  crs = 4326))
points_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(
  data.frame(lon = c(-99.1, -98.4, -97.7), lat = c(40.1, 40.3, 41.2)),
  coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)
denominator_sf <- sf::st_sf(
  population = c(5000, 8000),
  geometry = sf::st_sfc(
    sf::st_polygon(list(cbind(c(-100, -98.5, -98.5, -100, -100), c(39, 39, 42, 42, 39)))),
    sf::st_polygon(list(cbind(c(-98.5, -97, -97, -98.5, -98.5), c(39, 39, 42, 42, 39)))),
    crs = 4326))
mysterymaps_hex_bin_rate(boundary_sf, points_sf, denominator_sf, "population",
                         per = 1000, cellsize = 0.5)
}
